body: Where can you buy Vigor Boost? From the official website. At the time of writing, that's the only channel that publishes the 2, 3 and 6 bottle packages and backs orders with a 60-day money-back guarantee. Listings on Amazon, Walmart or eBay come from third parties, aren't covered by that guarantee, and can't be verified as genuine.

That might sound like a sales line. It isn't meant as one. In most supplement categories, buying from a random marketplace seller risks an expired bottle or a lost refund. In men's sexual health products, the risk is different in kind, and the FDA has spent years documenting it. We'll walk through why, what the official checkout looks like, and how to check a bottle once it's in your hands.
If you're still deciding whether to buy at all, start with our Vigor Boost review. This page assumes you've decided and want to buy it safely.
Where can you buy Vigor Boost?

The official Vigor Boost website, through its own order page. The buttons on this page lead there. It's a direct-to-consumer product, sold online and shipped to you, rather than one stocked on store shelves.

That model is common for supplements sold through online ads. It keeps the seller in control of pricing, packaging and refunds. The downside for you is that you can't pick it up at a pharmacy. The upside is that there's one place to buy it, which makes fakes easier to spot. Anything that isn't that place is, by definition, someone else.

You may find listings using the name, and you may also find completely unrelated products called Vigor Boost or something close to it. The name isn't unusual. Several different supplements and drinks use similar wording, and none of that tells you who made the bottle in the photo.

What we can say is this: the official seller publishes its packages and guarantee on its own site, and marketplace orders aren't covered by that guarantee. We can't verify where any marketplace seller sources stock, how it was stored, or whether it's the same product at all. If you're searching "Vigor Boost Amazon" because you want fast shipping or a familiar checkout, that's understandable. Just know you'd be trading the guarantee and the certainty of the source for it.

Marketplace reviews don't settle the question either. Star ratings on a listing can be carried over from an older or different product, and a page full of five-star reviews tells you nothing about who packed the bottle you'd receive. Read the photos instead: if a listing doesn't show a clear Supplement Facts panel that matches the one described further down this page, skip it.

Why does it matter where you buy a men's vitality gummy?

Because this is the category where tainted products are most common. The FDA runs a dedicated page on tainted sexual enhancement products and has listed hundreds of them over the years. The pattern is consistent. A product sold as "all natural" or "herbal" turns out, under lab testing, to contain sildenafil (the active ingredient in Viagra), tadalafil (Cialis) or chemical cousins of those drugs that were never approved at all.

Some of these come in forms that look harmless: honey packets, instant coffee, chocolates and candy-style products. A gummy fits right into that list. That's not a statement about Vigor Boost, whose label lists only botanicals, an amino acid and caffeine. It's a statement about what happens when the same name and picture can be printed on any bottle by anyone.

Counterfeiters target this category for obvious reasons. Demand is high, buyers are often embarrassed to ask questions, and a product that "works" because it secretly contains a prescription drug gets repeat customers. The cost lands on the buyer.
What are the risks of a counterfeit or tainted product?

The main danger is a hidden PDE5 inhibitor, the class of drug that includes sildenafil and tadalafil. On its own, under a doctor's care, that class is well studied. Hidden and unmeasured, it's a different story.

Nitrates. Men who take nitroglycerin or other nitrates for chest pain can't safely take PDE5 inhibitors. The combination can drop blood pressure to dangerous levels. A man who's been told not to take Viagra might take a "herbal" gummy and get the same drug anyway.
Unknown dose. Lab tests of tainted products have found drug amounts that vary from bottle to bottle, sometimes above the prescribed maximum.
Unapproved analogs. Some products contain drug-like compounds that were never tested in people at all.
Other blood pressure effects. Men on alpha-blockers or several blood pressure drugs are also at risk of a sharp drop.
No recourse. If something goes wrong, there's no seller to contact and no record of what you took.

Even the genuine Vigor Boost formula deserves a conversation with your doctor if you take nitrates, ED drugs or blood pressure medicine, since it contains L-arginine. Our page on Vigor Boost side effects and interactions covers that. A counterfeit simply removes the one thing you could check: the label.
Red flags: how to spot a fake Vigor Boost seller
Use this table before you pay. One red flag is a reason to slow down. Two or more is a reason to close the tab.
Price far below the official packages
Genuine stock rarely sells for a fraction of the published price

A classic setup for recurring charges; the official offer is a one-time charge
Claims to cure ED, add size or work "like Viagra"
No supplement can lawfully claim this; it suggests either fraud or a hidden drug
Botanicals don't work like that; a fast, strong effect is a warning sign of a hidden drug
No Supplement Facts panel in the photos
You can't compare it with the real label
Seller has no address or contact details
Payment by gift card, crypto or money-transfer app only
How do you make sure you're on the official Vigor Boost checkout?
A few checks take less than a minute:
Start from a trusted link. Use the button on a page you trust, or type the brand's site yourself, instead of clicking through a chain of ads and redirects.
Check the packages. You should see 2, 3 and 6 bottle options with the guarantee written out.
Look for a one-time charge. There should be no subscription, no auto-ship box pre-ticked, and no trial that converts later.
Check the address bar. The page should be on HTTPS, and the domain shouldn't change to something unrelated at the payment step.
Pay by credit card. It gives you the strongest dispute rights if something goes wrong.
Save proof. Screenshot the package, price and guarantee, and keep the confirmation email.

After you order, watch for two things. First, the confirmation email, which should show the package you chose and the total you agreed to. Second, your card statement. The charge may appear under a payment processor or company name rather than the words "Vigor Boost", which is normal for online stores. What isn't normal is a second charge you didn't approve, or a smaller recurring one a few weeks later. If you see either, contact the seller first, then your card issuer.

What should a genuine Vigor Boost bottle look like?
When the box arrives, compare the bottle with the details printed on the real label. Everything below should match.
Supplement Facts: serving size 1 gummy, 30 servings, 10 calories, 2 g total sugar (all added).
Proprietary blend: 82 mg, listing muira puama, ashwagandha, maca, catuaba, green tea extract, caffeine (10 mg), L-arginine, tribulus terrestris and horny goat weed.
Other ingredients: corn syrup, cane sugar, water, apple pectin, sorbitol, natural flavors, citric acid and sodium citrate.
Claims: "Supports men's vitality" with the standard FDA disclaimer, and a note that it's produced in a GMP facility.
Seal: intact under the cap. The label says not to use it if the seal is broken or missing.

If the label shows other ingredients, a different distributor, or claims about treating erectile dysfunction, don't take it. A bottle labeled HorseBoost is a different product from a different distributor, even though it shares the same blend; our Vigor Boost vs Horse Boost comparison explains the differences.
What if you already bought Vigor Boost somewhere else?
Don't panic, and don't take it until you've checked it.
Compare the bottle against the label details above, line by line.
If anything doesn't match, or the seal is broken, set it aside. Contact the marketplace for a refund under its own buyer-protection policy.

If you've taken it and felt a strong, fast effect, a headache, flushing, vision changes or dizziness, those are signs commonly associated with hidden PDE5 drugs. Stop and talk to a doctor, especially if you take any heart or blood pressure medicine.
Report suspected fakes or bad reactions to the FDA through its MedWatch program. Reports are how tainted products end up on the FDA's warning list.
Should you see a doctor before buying any men's vitality product?

If what's driving the purchase is a change in erections, yes. New or persistent erection problems can be an early sign of heart disease, diabetes or low testosterone. A doctor can check for those and, if appropriate, prescribe a medication with a known dose from a real pharmacy, which is the opposite of the tainted-product gamble. Vigor Boost isn't an ED treatment, and it isn't meant to replace one.
If you're after general energy and stamina and your health is otherwise good, the official site is the place to buy. For more reading on men's health topics, see our men's health section.
Bottom line: where to buy Vigor Boost

Buy it from the official website, nowhere else. You get the published packages, a one-time charge and a 60-day money-back guarantee, and you know the bottle came from the named distributor. In a category where some "herbal" products have turned out to contain prescription drugs, that certainty is worth more than a faster delivery from a marketplace.
faq: Is Vigor Boost sold at Walmart, CVS or GNC?

Not through any channel the official seller lists. Vigor Boost is sold direct to consumers through its official website. Any store or marketplace listing is a third party, and its orders aren't covered by the official 60-day guarantee.
Why is Vigor Boost cheaper on some websites?

Usually because it isn't the official checkout. A lower price can mean old stock, a different product with a similar name, a counterfeit, or a trial offer that turns into recurring charges. None of those come with the official guarantee.
Can I buy just one bottle of Vigor Boost?

At the time of writing, the official order page sells packages of 2, 3 or 6 bottles. A single-bottle offer is a sign you may not be on the official checkout, so check the page carefully before paying.
Does Vigor Boost ship outside the US?
Check the official order page for current shipping destinations and costs. The free shipping on the 3 and 6 bottle packages applies to US orders at the time of writing.
Is there a Vigor Boost coupon code?
We haven't seen an official coupon program. Sites advertising Vigor Boost coupon codes often use them to draw clicks. The published package discounts on the official page are the real savings.
How do I report a fake Vigor Boost product?
Contact the seller or marketplace first for a refund, then report it to the FDA through MedWatch, especially if you had a reaction. You can also contact the distributor listed on the genuine label.
How long does Vigor Boost shipping take?
Delivery times are set by the seller and depend on your location. The confirmation email should include tracking details. Check the official order page for current estimates.
